question: The National Logistics Policy in India was launched in_________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2022**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Logistics Policy (NLP)** in India was launched on **17 September 2022**, by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** during an event held in **New Delhi**.
 
• The policy aims to address challenges in India’s **logistics sector** and reduce costs, making the sector more competitive globally.
 
• The primary goal of the **NLP** is to bring down the **logistics cost** in India to **8% of GDP** from the current 13-14%, aligning with developed nations.
 
• It provides a **comprehensive framework** for the development of the logistics ecosystem in India, integrating various logistics-related initiatives.
 
• The policy focuses on areas such as **infrastructure improvement, digital transformation, skill development**, and streamlining regulatory processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Logistics Sector in India:**

 
 
• The logistics sector contributes around **5% of India’s GDP** and employs more than **22 million people**.
 
• India ranked **44th** in the **Logistics Performance Index (LPI) 2018** published by the World Bank, highlighting the need for improvement in this sector.
 
• The sector is fragmented, with a significant share being unorganized, posing challenges in terms of efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
 
 
 
• **Components of the National Logistics Policy:**
 
 
• It integrates initiatives like **PM Gati Shakti**, which focuses on multimodal infrastructure connectivity.
 
• The policy is supported by a **Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP)**, ensuring digital integration across various ministries and stakeholders.
 
• Introduction of the **Ease of Logistics (E-Logs) portal** to resolve issues faced by industry stakeholders in a transparent manner.
 
• Emphasis on the development of **Multimodal Logistics Parks (MMLPs)** to facilitate integrated transportation and reduce costs.
 
 
 
• **Significance of NLP:**
 
 
• Helps improve **India’s global trade competitiveness** by reducing logistics costs and improving efficiency.
 
• Supports the government's vision of making India a **global manufacturing hub** under the **Make in India** initiative.
 
• Encourages private sector participation in logistics infrastructure development.
 
• Promotes **sustainability** by enhancing green logistics practices and reducing carbon emissions.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in India’s Logistics Sector:**
 
 
• High **logistics costs** compared to global standards.
 
• Fragmented infrastructure and lack of integration among **transport modes**.
 
• Regulatory hurdles and inefficiencies in supply chain management.
 
• Dependence on road transport, leading to **higher costs and environmental issues**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **PM Gati Shakti:** Launched in **October 2021**, it is a **National Master Plan** for multimodal connectivity, aiming to improve infrastructure planning and reduce logistics costs.
 
• **Logistics Performance Index (LPI):** Published by the **World Bank**, it evaluates countries based on their logistics performance across indicators like infrastructure, customs, and international shipments.
 
• **India’s Target:** To achieve a **$5 trillion economy**, reducing logistics costs is pivotal for improving trade and manufacturing competitiveness.
 
• **Multimodal Logistics Parks (MMLPs):** These are being developed under the **Bharatmala Pariyojana** to enhance the integration of different modes of transport.
 
• **Digital Transformation:** Platforms like **ULIP** and **E-Logs** aim to streamline processes and reduce bureaucratic inefficiencies in the logistics sector.
